problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Shipment Alpha: size 47 cubic meters
* Shipment Beta: size 48 cubic meters
* Shipment Gamma: size 58 cubic meters
* Shipment Delta: size 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Epsilon: size 63 cubic meters
* Shipment Zeta: size 56 cubic meters
* Shipment Eta: size 61 cubic meters
* Shipment Theta: size 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Iota: size 47 cubic meters
* Shipment Kappa: size 63 cubic meters
* Shipment Lambda: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment Mu: size 58 cubic meters
* Shipment Nu: size 64 cubic meters
* Shipment Xi: size 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Omicron: size 55 cubic meters
* Shipment Pi: size 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Rho: size 55 cubic meters
* Shipment Sigma: size 47 cubic meters
* Shipment Tau: size 30 cubic meters
* Shipment Upsilon: size 43 cubic meters
* Shipment Phi: size 59 cubic meters
* Shipment Chi: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment Psi: size 55 cubic meters
* Shipment Omega: size 57 cubic meters
* Shipment A1: size 38 cubic meters
* Shipment B1: size 41 cubic meters
* Shipment C1: size 60 cubic meters
* Shipment D1: size 42 cubic meters
* Shipment E1: size 40 cubic meters
* Shipment F1: size 69 cubic meters

Each cargo plane can carry up to 100 cubic meters of total shipment volume. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes possible. Every shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume assigned to a plane cannot exceed its capacity.
